overview: Anta Sports is China's largest sportswear group and the third-largest globally by market capitalization, operating a multi-brand portfolio spanning mass-market performance sports (ANTA), premium sports fashion (FILA), and high-end outdoor/performance brands (DESCENTE, KOLON SPORT, JACK WOLFSKIN, MAIA ACTIVE). The company is also the largest and controlling shareholder of NYSE-listed Amer Sports (owner of Arc'teryx, Salomon, Wilson, Peak Performance, and Atomic) and, as of October 2026, completed a EUR1.5 billion (~USD1.8 billion) purchase of a 29.06% stake in Germany's PUMA SE, becoming its largest shareholder. Revenue (RMB80.2bn in FY2025) is overwhelmingly China-domestic, generated through a DTC-centered hybrid retail/wholesale model across roughly 13,000 monobrand stores plus a fast-growing e-commerce channel (~36% of sales), with an emerging overseas push led by Southeast Asia, the Middle East, and a first North American flagship (Beverly Hills, early 2026).

business_model.summary: Vertically integrated design, R&D, manufacturing (hybrid in-house/outsourced), marketing and retail of branded footwear, apparel and accessories, monetized through a DTC-centered hybrid distribution model (direct retail plus wholesale/franchise). Revenue mix has diversified rapidly: ANTA (mass-market) still largest at ~43% of FY2025 revenue but growing slowest (+3.7% YoY); FILA (premium sports fashion) ~35.5% (+6.9%); 'All other brands' (DESCENTE, KOLON SPORT, JACK WOLFSKIN, MAIA ACTIVE) now ~21.2% and the fastest-growing segment (+59.2% YoY, aided by the Jack Wolfskin acquisition completed May 2025). Group gross margin ~62%, operating margin ~23.8% (FY2025), both best-in-class versus global peers. The group also holds large non-consolidated equity stakes in Amer Sports (NYSE: AS, largest shareholder, consortium-controlled) and, since October 2026, a 29.06% stake in PUMA SE, both accounted for as associates/investments rather than consolidated revenue.

revenue_streams.name: All other brands (DESCENTE, KOLON SPORT, Jack Wolfskin, Maia Active)

business_model.customer_type: B2C (mass-market to premium consumer retail), both direct retail (DTC) and wholesale/franchise distributors
business_model.geographic_mix: Overwhelmingly Mainland China/Greater China (>95% of consolidated revenue); overseas expansion nascent but accelerating (Southeast Asia 'Thousand Stores Plan' by 2028, Middle East/Africa, North America flagship opened 2026); e-commerce ~35.8% of Group revenue

main_competitors: Puma (now a strategic investee, not purely a competitor)
competitive_position.market_position: Largest sportswear company in China by revenue and retail sales, with domestic market share of 21.8% in 2025 (up from 20.8% in 2024) per management-cited third-party data; among the top three sportswear groups globally by market cap, behind Nike, ahead of Adidas in some periods

moat_factors.description: Differentiated brand positioning (mass to premium, performance to lifestyle to outdoor) captures multiple price points and consumer segments simultaneously, a structure competitors like Li Ning and Xtep have not replicated at scale

In-house manufacturing for a portion of footwear/apparel plus a shared-services platform (supply chain, digitalization, finance, HR) across brands drives cost and operating efficiency unmatched by single-brand domestic peers
~13,000 monobrand stores and deep membership/e-commerce data support targeted merchandising and inventory discipline (inventory turnover improved, trade payables/receivables tightly managed)

Demonstrated ability to scale acquired/licensed brands (FILA China to >RMB30bn retail sales, DESCENTE and KOLON SPORT each crossing RMB10bn) under a 'brand-centric governance' model that preserves brand autonomy while sharing back-office scale
Net cash position (RMB31.7bn at FY2025-end, RMB39.1bn at H1 2026) funded the PUMA stake purchase entirely from internal cash, a flexibility few peers have

weaknesses: Heavy reliance on the Chinese consumer and domestic retail cycle; limited international consolidated revenue to date
Core ANTA brand growth has slowed to low-single digits, now reliant on FILA and smaller brands for growth
Complex, sprawling multi-entity ownership structure (Anta International, Amer Sports, PUMA stake) makes look-through economics and governance harder for investors to assess
E-commerce mix shift (now ~36% of revenue) is structurally dilutive to gross margin
No management/operational control over PUMA (minority stake, no current plan for a full takeover) limits ability to extract synergies quickly

growth_drivers: Continued share gains from international brands in China as 'domestic brand' sentiment and localized product/marketing resonate with Chinese consumers
Scaling of DESCENTE, KOLON SPORT and newly acquired Jack Wolfskin in the outdoor/performance segment, now the fastest-growing part of the business (+59% YoY in FY2025)

Globalization strategy: Southeast Asia 'Thousand Stores Plan' (1,000 ANTA points of sale by 2028), expansion into the Middle East/Africa, India (via Brandman Retail partnership), and first North American flagship store (Beverly Hills, 2026)
E-commerce and livestream/content commerce growth, plus the AI365 strategy (AI-assisted design, digital-human livestreaming, AI customer service) targeting cost efficiency and incremental GMV

Strategic stakes in Amer Sports (Arc'teryx, Salomon, Wilson) and now PUMA SE (29.06%, completed October 2026) extend ANTA's reach into premium global/outdoor and European-heritage sports brands, with potential for commercial collaboration (e.g., China distribution/retail synergies) without full consolidation risk
Continued margin expansion via premiumization, R&D-led product innovation (R&D spend up ~5x since 2016, 4,569 patents), and disciplined channel/inventory management
Capital return program: ongoing share buybacks (HKD1.7bn in FY2025, HKD2.96bn cumulative 2024-25) and rising dividend payout (~50% of adjusted profit)

business.description: ANTA segment revenue growth has slowed to +3.7% in FY2025 and low-single-digit retail sales growth through H1/Q3 2026, raising reliance on other segments to sustain group growth

Nike and Adidas are stabilizing/recovering in Greater China (Adidas posted multiple consecutive quarters of China growth); domestic rivals Li Ning, Xtep and 361 Degrees compete aggressively on price and in overlapping segments

The vast majority of consolidated revenue and profit is generated in Mainland China; a slowdown in Chinese consumer discretionary spending disproportionately affects the group versus globally diversified peers

Jack Wolfskin (completed May 2025) is in an early five-year revitalization plan; Maia Active remains in an incubation/loss-making phase; integration execution on both, plus managing a large minority stake in PUMA without operational control, carries execution risk
Online channel now ~36% of revenue and carries structurally lower gross margins than offline retail, pressuring blended gross margin

financial.risk: Large cash deployment into non-controlling stakes
financial.description: The PUMA stake (EUR1.5bn) was funded entirely from internal cash; while the balance sheet remains net-cash, continued large minority-stake purchases reduce capital available for buybacks/dividends or organic reinvestment and carry mark-to-market/equity-method earnings volatility

PUMA stake is EUR-denominated and Amer Sports exposure is USD/multi-currency, while ANTA reports in RMB; currency translation can create volatility in reported equity-method income and investment valuation even though core operations are RMB-functional

Gains/losses from Amer Sports and (going forward) PUMA equity accounting have already caused one-off swings in reported profit attributable to shareholders (e.g., FY2024 included a large one-off gain from Amer Sports equity dilution/listing, flattering the headline YoY comparison against FY2025's 'clean' adjusted profit growth)

regulatory.description: The PUMA stake required regulatory clearance (reported China antitrust approval) and the Amer Sports consortium structure remains subject to ongoing regulatory and governance scrutiny in both China and the US/Europe given the scale of outbound Chinese capital

regulatory.risk: China consumer/retail regulation and data rules
regulatory.description: E-commerce, advertising, and data-privacy regulation in China could affect marketing practices, online channel economics, and AI-driven personalization initiatives

macro.description: Despite resilient 2025 GDP growth (~5.0%) and record total retail sales (RMB50.1 trillion, +3.7% YoY), China's broader consumer recovery has been described by management as 'rational' rather than robust; a sharper slowdown would hit discretionary apparel/footwear spending directly
RMB movements affect translation of overseas investments (PUMA/Amer Sports) and the relative cost of imported materials/technology, as well as HKD-denominated dividend payouts

US-China and broader geopolitical tensions could affect sourcing, overseas expansion (including the new North American flagship), and the optics/approval of Chinese capital acquiring stakes in Western brands (Amer Sports, PUMA)

macro_factors.industry_outlook: China sportswear market remains a structural growth category within consumer retail, with outdoor sports participation (400m+ participants) outpacing traditional apparel; 2025 Chinese GDP grew ~5.0% and total retail sales of consumer goods topped RMB50 trillion for the first time; sportswear/outdoor segment has been a bright spot even as broader consumer sentiment stays cautious ('rational consumption', pursuit of 'emotional value')
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - discretionary consumer spending category, but Anta's multi-brand/multi-price-point architecture and DTC inventory discipline provide more resilience than single-brand peers; company has delivered 12 consecutive years of revenue growth through multiple macro cycles
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct (net cash position reduces financing cost sensitivity); moderate indirect via Chinese consumer credit conditions and property-market wealth effects on discretionary spending

recent_developments.event: Completed the acquisition of a 29.06% stake in PUMA SE from the Pinault family's Artemis vehicle for approximately EUR1.5 billion (~USD1.8bn) in cash, funded entirely from internal resources, making ANTA PUMA's largest shareholder; ANTA stated no current plan for a full takeover offer and intends to seek board representation

H1 2026 revenue grew 12.9% YoY to RMB43.5bn, operating profit +16.1% to RMB11.76bn, profit attributable to shareholders +34.9% to RMB9.49bn; net cash position rose to RMB39.1bn; 'All other brands' segment revenue +44.2% YoY, continuing to outpace ANTA (+4.8%) and FILA (+6.1%)

Quarterly operational updates showed ANTA core brand retail sales growth slowing to low-single digits, FILA at low-to-mid-single digits, while 'other brands' (DESCENTE, KOLON SPORT, Jack Wolfskin) continued strong 20%+ growth, consistent with management's full-year guidance
ANTA equipped 13 national teams at the Milan Winter Olympics, reinforcing brand visibility and technology positioning ahead of China's 15th National Games sponsorship
Opened first ANTA flagship store in North America (Beverly Hills, Los Angeles), marking formal entry into a premium Western retail market
Completed acquisition of German outdoor brand Jack Wolfskin, broadening the outdoor portfolio from mass to premium; management laid out a five-year global revitalization plan for the brand

Revenue surpassed RMB80 billion for the first time (+13.3% YoY), 12th consecutive year of growth; China sportswear market share rose to 21.8% (from 20.8%); gross margin softened slightly to 62.0% (from 62.2%) on e-commerce mix and quality investment, but operating margin improved to 23.8% (from 23.4%)

FY2024 profit attributable to shareholders included a one-off gain from the Amer Sports Listing and Placing equity dilution, inflating the headline figure (RMB15.6bn) versus FY2025's 'clean' RMB13.6bn; on an adjusted basis (excluding one-offs), profit grew 13.9% YoY in FY2025

guidance.as_of: Interim Report 2026 (H1 2026, reported August 2026) and FY2025 Annual Report (March 2026)

items.notes: Consistent with Q1-Q3 2026 operational updates; reflects a maturing core brand in a competitive mass-market segment
Management cited 'ONE FILA' strategy execution and product/retail refinement as supporting continued steady growth

items.metric: All other brands retail sales growth
items.notes: DESCENTE and KOLON SPORT framed as the Group's dedicated 'growth brands'; Jack Wolfskin and Maia Active remain in incubation with resources continuing to be allocated for brand-building rather than near-term margin

items.target: ANTA 7,000-7,100 / ANTA KIDS 2,500-2,600 / FILA (incl. KIDS/FUSION) 1,900-2,000 / DESCENTE 260-270 / KOLON SPORT 220-230 / MAIA ACTIVE 60-70
items.notes: Store counts for ANTA and FILA family brands are being rationalized/optimized (roughly flat to slightly down) while growth brands continue modest net store additions

items.target: ~50% of adjusted profit attributable to equity shareholders
items.notes: FY2025 payout was 50.1%; H1 2026 payout ratio 50.3%, continuing the long-standing policy

items.target: 1,000 ANTA points of sale across Southeast Asia
items.notes: Part of the 'ANTA Southeast Asia Thousand Stores Plan,' framed as the globalization strategy's bridgehead before expansion into South Asia, Australia/New Zealand and India

guidance.management_commentary: Co-CEOs characterized 2026 as a year of continued execution of the 'Single-focus, Multi-brand, Globalization' strategy, with ANTA and FILA as 'cornerstone brands' prioritizing operational efficiency and inventory discipline, and DESCENTE/KOLON SPORT as 'growth brands' sustaining rapid expansion. Chairman Ding Shizhong emphasized a multi-decade (10/20/30-year) ambition for 'genuine global influence,' framing the Jack Wolfskin and PUMA transactions as long-term strategic investments rather than scale-chasing M&A. Management flagged 2026 domestic macro uncertainty but expects China's 15th Five-Year Plan domestic-demand policies to underpin a 'stable and sizeable' sportswear market, with outdoor sports the fastest-growing sub-segment.

bull_case: Best-in-class execution among Chinese consumer brands: 12 consecutive years of revenue growth, rising China market share (21.8% in 2025), and industry-leading operating margins (~24%) through a disciplined multi-brand model

Diversified, de-risked growth engine: as ANTA core brand matures, FILA and the fast-growing 'other brands' segment (DESCENTE, KOLON SPORT, Jack Wolfskin) are scaling into meaningful profit contributors, reducing single-brand dependency

Optionality from strategic stakes in Amer Sports and now PUMA provides exposure to premium global/outdoor brands and potential commercial synergies (China distribution, product/marketing know-how) without full consolidation balance-sheet risk

Fortress balance sheet (net cash of RMB31.7bn at FY2025-end, RMB39.1bn at H1 2026) funds M&A, buybacks (HKD2.96bn since 2024) and a ~50% payout ratio simultaneously, with low financial leverage (gearing ~18-19%)

Secular tailwinds in Chinese outdoor/sports participation (400m+ participants) and domestic-brand share gains versus Nike/Adidas support a multi-year runway, while globalization (Southeast Asia, Middle East, North America) offers a long-dated option on international growth
bear_case: Core ANTA brand growth has slowed to low-single digits, and the business remains overwhelmingly dependent on the Chinese consumer; a sharper China consumption slowdown would hit the group harder than globally diversified peers like Nike or Adidas

Rising competitive intensity as Adidas stabilizes in Greater China and domestic rivals (Li Ning, Xtep, 361 Degrees) compete aggressively on price and channel, compressing category-wide growth and promotional discipline

Complex, sprawling corporate structure (Anta International consortium, Amer Sports stake, new PUMA minority stake) makes look-through valuation and capital-allocation discipline harder to assess, and large non-controlling stake purchases (PUMA, EUR1.5bn) divert cash without operational control or guaranteed synergies

Reported profit comparability is noisy: FY2024's headline profit was inflated by a one-off Amer Sports equity-dilution gain, and further mark-to-market or equity-accounting swings from Amer Sports/PUMA stakes could continue to distort year-over-year growth narratives

Margin headwinds from e-commerce mix shift (now ~36% of revenue, structurally lower-margin) and continued heavy investment (R&D, advertising, new-brand incubation for Jack Wolfskin and Maia Active) could pressure margins if top-line growth disappoints
